title: Targeted Extraction using `id` and `class_`
instructions: Practice using BeautifulSoup to extract data by targeting specific `id` and `class` attributes from an HTML document.
steps: **Task 1:** Import the `BeautifulSoup` class from the `bs4` module.
**Task 2:** Create a BeautifulSoup object called `soup` from `html_doc` using `'html.parser'`.
**Task 3:** Use `soup.find()` to locate the element with the ID `main-title`. Store it in `main_title` and print its text content.
**Task 4:** Use `soup.find_all()` to locate all elements with the class `product-name`. Store the result in `product_names`.
**Task 5:** Loop through `product_names` and print the `.text` of each element.
starterCode:
# Task 1: Import BeautifulSoup html_doc = """

Daily Deals on Electronics

Laptop X

Mouse Pro

Monitor 4K

""" # Task 2: Initialize BeautifulSoup soup = ??? # Task 3: Find and print the main title by ID main_title = ??? print(f"Main Title: {???}") # Task 4: Find all product names by class product_names = ??? # Task 5: Loop through and print all product names for name in product_names:
solution:
# Task 1: Import BeautifulSoup from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html_doc = """

Daily Deals on Electronics

Laptop X

Mouse Pro

Monitor 4K

""" # Task 2: Initialize BeautifulSoup soup = BeautifulSoup(html_doc, 'html.parser') # Task 3: Find and print the main title by ID main_title = soup.find(id='main-title') print(f"Main Title: {main_title.text}") # Task 4: Find all product names by class product_names = soup.find_all(class_='product-name') # Task 5: Loop through and print all product names for name in product_names: print(name.text)
hints: **Task 4:** Finding by class uses `class_=` (note the underscore!): `soup.find_all(class_='product-name')`
**Task 5:** Inside the loop, `name.text` gives just the text content.
